title: The day the sky went dark at noon 🌑
subject: smoke
description:
Would you have thought it was the end of the world? 👇

On May 19, 1780, darkness fell across New England at midday. Candles were lit by noon, roosters crowed in the afternoon, and some believed Judgment Day had come. In 2008, University of Missouri tree-ring researchers traced it to huge wildfires in Ontario, combined with fog and cloud.

Sources: University of Missouri ("Fire Scars Reveal Source of New England's 1780 Dark Day", 2008), McMurry et al., International Journal of Wildland Fire (2007), Wikipedia ("New England's Dark Day", "Abraham Davenport"), National Weather Service (June 2023 wildfire smoke)

scenes.text: The sky went dark at noon.
On May 19, 1780, darkness spread from Maine to New Jersey. At Harvard, it peaked at 12:45 p.m.
People ate lunch by candlelight. In Ipswich, roosters crowed at 2 in the afternoon.
Connecticut lawmakers feared Judgment Day. Abraham Davenport reportedly said, "I choose to be found doing my duty."
In 2008, Missouri researchers found the cause in tree rings: massive wildfires in Ontario.
In June 2023, Canadian smoke turned New York's afternoon sky orange.
